mainTopic: חזקה in a married woman's property, and whether a husband's sale of a field to his wife is valid
overview: The גמרא finishes a dispute about making a חזקה in a married woman's property. רב rules like the דייני גולה, then explains to his students that he only meant this in רב יוסף's case. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's rule that a wife cannot make a חזקה in her husband's fields: it applies even when he gave her a different field for her support. The גמרא then asks whether a husband who 'sells' a field to his wife might only want to uncover her hidden money. It shows that the משנה's 'proof' can mean a gift document. רב נחמן then rules that a sale to one's wife is valid. רב הונא challenges this as obvious, and the debate turns to whether a sale document alone acquires land, using שמואל's rule and רב המנונא's ברייתא. The גמרא then defends רב נחמן against a ברייתא about loans from a slave or wife: a loan is different, because no one wants to be 'servant to the lender.' The amud ends as רב הונא בר אבין begins a ruling on the same case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The judges of the exile allow a חזקה, and רב rules like them
steps.stepSummary: The דייני גולה hold that one can make a חזקה here, and רב says the הלכה follows them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The judges of the exile said: one can make a חזקה. רב said: the הלכה follows the judges of the exile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a dispute that began before this point: the דייני גולה say a חזקה can work here. רב then rules that the הלכה follows them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, an opinion held that one cannot make a חזקה in a married woman's property. The דייני גולה disagree and say one can. רב sides with the דייני גולה, which sounds surprising, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The judges of the exile (the judges of בבל)
One can establish a חזקה (a claim of ownership based on use)

phrases.english: But the judges of the exile said:
One can establish a חזקה.
רב said: The halacha follows the judges of the exile.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה can be made here, and the הלכה follows the דייני גולה.

steps.title: רב's students ask if he changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי ask רב whether he has taken back his earlier ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: Has the master taken back his ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: רב's students notice that this ruling seems to clash with what רב said before. They ask him whether he has changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב had ruled that one cannot make a חזקה in a married woman's property. Ruling now like the דייני גולה looks like the opposite. The question is really a challenge: how can both rulings stand?

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted, took back his view
Master (a respectful way to address a teacher)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
Has the master retracted his ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 1 by pointing to his own earlier ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling like the דייני גולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב said earlier that there is no חזקה in a married woman's property, so ruling now that there is one looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: רב explains: their view is reasonable, like רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב says he only meant that the דייני גולה's view makes sense in a certain case, the one רב יוסף described.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I said it is reasonable, in line with רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that he did not take back his ruling. He only meant that the דייני גולה's view makes sense in a limited case, the case רב יוסף spoke about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's basic rule stays in place: normally there is no חזקה in a married woman's property. The דייני גולה are right only for the situation רב יוסף described, where someone uses the land for three years after the husband has died. So the two rulings do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense

phrases.english: He said to them: I said it is reasonable –
like Rav Yosef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by narrowing step 1 to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב reversed himself and now holds a חזקה always works in a married woman's property.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's basic rule stands. The דייני גולה are correct only in the case רב יוסף described.
steps.whatToRemember: רב did not change his mind. He agreed with the דייני גולה only for רב יוסף's case, where the land is used for three years after the husband dies.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say a wife cannot make a חזקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks why it needs to say this, since a wife eats from her husband's fields as part of her support anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "And a wife has no חזקה in her husband's property, etc." That is obvious! Since she is entitled to support, it is her support that she is eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה: a wife cannot make a חזקה in her husband's property. It asks why this needs saying at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband must provide his wife with מזונות. So when she eats the produce of his field, that is simply her support. It is not a sign that she owns the field, which makes the משנה's rule seem obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Food and support a husband owes his wife

phrases.english: "And not for a wife with regard to her husband's property, etc."
That is obvious!
Since she has a right to support,
it is her support that she is eating!

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a wife has no חזקה in her husband's property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her eating is already explained by her right to support, so the rule seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The rule applies even to a second field
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a case where the husband gave her a different field for support, and she used another one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for where he set aside a different piece of land for her support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a special case. The husband set aside one field for her support, and she ate from a different field for three years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case, her support cannot explain her eating from the second field, since her support comes from another field. Even so, the משנה teaches that she still does not make a חזקה in it. That is the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed except for... (this is the case it comes to teach)

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he designated another piece of land for her support.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּיַחֵד לַהּ אַרְעָא אַחֲרִיתִי לִמְזוֹנַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 4 by pointing to a case that is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a case that is not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If she has her own support field, eating from another field should show she owns it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even then, she makes no חזקה in her husband's other field.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife cannot make a חזקה in her husband's field, even when her support comes from a different field.

steps.title: How can a wife's proof ever work?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה implies that with proof she can keep the field. But the husband could say he only sold it to uncover her hidden money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that with proof, she does keep it? But let him say he only wanted to uncover her money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely: no חזקה works for her, but proof would. It then challenges this, because even a sale document could be explained away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband might claim he never truly meant to sell. He only offered to sell so that she would pay him, and he would find out she had hidden money. If that claim works, even her proof should not help her.

phrases.english: But with proof – she has a claim?
Let him say that he wanted to expose hidden money!
phrases.notes: The husband would say he only pretended to sell, to see if she would come up with money she was hiding.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רְאָיָה – יֵשׁ? לֵימָא לְגַלּוֹיֵי זוּזֵי הוּא דְּבָעֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a wife with proof keeps her husband's field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband can say the sale was fake, done only to uncover her hidden money, so proof should not help.

steps.title: Can we learn that a sale to a wife is valid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning from the משנה that a husband's sale of a field to his wife works, and he cannot claim he only wanted to uncover her money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you learn from this that if a man sells a field to his wife she has acquired it, and we do not say he only wanted to uncover her money?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to turn the משנה's hint into a proof for a wider rule: a sale from husband to wife is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If proof helps the wife, the משנה seems to reject the claim of uncovering money. That would mean any sale of a field from a husband to his wife is valid. The גמרא puts this forward to see whether it holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sells a field to his wife

phrases.english: Can you conclude from this
that one who sells a field to his wife – she has acquired it,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָמְרִינַן: לְגַלּוֹיֵי זוּזֵי הוּא דְּבָעֵי?!
phrases.english: and we do not say that he wanted to expose hidden money?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ, הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֶה לְאִשְׁתּוֹ – קָנְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the inference from step 6 into a suggested general rule.
steps.raayaObject: A husband's sale of a field to his wife is valid, and the claim of uncovering money is rejected.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's hint that a wife with proof keeps her husband's field.

steps.title: No: the proof the משנה means is a gift document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה is talking about a שטר מתנה, where the uncovering-money claim does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Say that "she has proof" means with a gift document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from step 7. The משנה's "proof" means a gift document, not a sale document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a gift, the husband took no money, so he cannot claim he was trying to uncover her money. That means the משנה says nothing about a sale. So this משנה cannot prove whether a sale to a wife works; רב נחמן rules on that in the next step.

phrases.english: No; say:
that "she has proof" refers to a deed of gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; אֵימָא: הָא רְאָיָה יֵשׁ – בִּשְׁטַר מַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7, and also answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning a rule about sales from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's proof can be a gift document, where no money changed hands, so it tells us nothing about sales.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's "proof" for a wife is a שטר מתנה. Whether a husband's sale to his wife is valid is not proven from here.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not learn from the משנה that a sale to one's wife is valid, because the משנה can be read as talking about a gift. That a sale is valid comes from רב נחמן in the next step, not from the משנה.

steps.title: רב נחמן shares a great teaching about selling a field to one's wife
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells רב הונא that the night before they taught: a man who sells a field to his wife, she owns it, and we don't say he only wanted to uncover her money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא: You weren't with us last night in the study hall inside the town, where we said a great teaching. רב הונא asked: What great teaching did you say? רב נחמן said: If a man sells a field to his wife, she owns it, and we don't say he only wanted to uncover her hidden money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story in which רב נחמן reports a new rule to רב הונא. The sale of a field to one's wife is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw the worry that a husband might 'sell' to his wife only to find out where she hid her money. רב נחמן rules that we don't suspect this, so the sale stands. This short exchange sets up the discussion that follows about why this rule is new.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the town boundary (the study hall there)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Huna:
The Master was not with us
in the evening, within the town boundary,
phrases.notes: He means the study hall that was inside the town.

phrases.english: where we said great teachings.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי מִילֵּי מְעַלְּיָיתָא אָמְרִיתוּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: What great teachings did you say?
One who sells a field to his wife – she has acquired it,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָמְרִינַן לְגַלּוֹיֵי זוּזֵי הוּא דְּבָעֵי.
phrases.english: and we do not say that he just wanted to uncover the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the uncovering-money worry from step 6 and gives a clear ruling from רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband's sale of a field to his wife is valid; we don't assume he only wanted to uncover her money.

steps.title: רב הונא says the rule is obvious because a document alone buys land
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the rule is obvious: even ignoring the money, she acquires with the שטר, as the משנה teaches land can be bought with money, a document, or taking possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: That's obvious! Take the money out of the picture, and she acquires through the document. Didn't we learn: Land can be acquired with money, with a document, or with taking possession?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges רב נחמן: why call this a great teaching? It seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about uncovering money only matters if the money is needed to complete the sale. But a שטר alone can complete a purchase of land. So even if the money is ignored, the wife owns the field through the document, and nothing new was taught.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that serves as a guarantee (land)
Money, document, taking possession: the three ways to acquire land

phrases.english: He said to him: That is obvious,
remove the money from here – and let her acquire through the document!
Didn't we learn in a משנה:
Property that serves as a guarantee
is acquired by money, by a document, and by taking possession?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the newness of רב נחמן's ruling in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that his ruling is a great new teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שטר alone acquires land, so the money (and the worry about uncovering it) doesn't matter; the ruling is obvious.

steps.title: שמואל limits the document rule to gifts
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers with שמואל's rule: a שטר alone works only for a gift; for a sale, the buyer doesn't acquire until he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: But wasn't it said about that משנה, שמואל said: They only taught this about a gift document. But with a sale document, the buyer doesn't acquire until he pays the price.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his teaching by showing that a sale document alone is not enough. So the money does matter in a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, in a sale the payment is needed to complete the purchase. So the worry that the husband only wanted to uncover her money is a real issue. That makes רב נחמן's ruling that the sale still works a real חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said about it (a teaching stated on that source)

phrases.english: He said to him: But wasn't it said about it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטַר מַתָּנָה,
phrases.english: Shmuel said: They taught this only about a gift document,
but with a sale document – he does not acquire
until he gives him its price?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the משנה's document rule applies only to gifts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שטר alone completes any purchase of land, so the money doesn't matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a sale, payment is needed, so the money matters and רב נחמן's ruling is new.

steps.title: רב המנונא's challenge: a sale document works on its own
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings רב המנונא's challenge from a ברייתא that says writing 'my field is sold to you' on paper or clay completes the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב המנונא challenge this: How is acquiring with a document done? If he wrote for him on paper or on clay, even if it isn't worth a פרוטה, 'My field is sold to you' or 'My field is acquired by you,' then it is sold or given?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back against שמואל's rule with a ברייתא that seems to say a sale document alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions 'sold to you' and says the field is sold, with no mention of paying. That seems to show a sale document works without money, against שמואל. If so, רב הונא's point returns: רב נחמן's ruling is obvious.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Hamnuna raise a challenge:
phrases.notes: The text doesn't say who is speaking; it's רב הונא answering רב נחמן.

phrases.english: With a document – how is it done?

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב לוֹ עַל הַנְּיָיר אוֹ עַל הַחֶרֶס –
phrases.english: If he wrote for him on paper or on clay –

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה:
phrases.english: even though it is not worth a peruta:
"My field is sold to you," "My field is acquired by you" –
it is thereby sold and given?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's limit brought in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a sale document alone does not acquire
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a document reading 'my field is sold to you' completes the sale, with no payment mentioned.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about selling a poor field
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רב המנונא himself resolved his challenge: the ברייתא is about someone selling his field because it is poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't he himself raise the challenge and he himself answer it: The ברייתא is about one who sells his field because it is poor?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends שמואל's rule and his own teaching. The ברייתא is a special case, so a normal sale still needs payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person selling a poor field wants to get rid of it quickly, so he lets the document alone complete the sale. In a normal sale, the buyer doesn't own the field until he pays. So the money matters, and רב נחמן's ruling that a wife's purchase is valid really is a חידוש.
steps.whatToRemember: By שמואל's rule, a sale of land normally needs payment, not just a שטר. That is why רב נחמן's ruling is new: a husband's sale to his wife is valid, and we don't suspect he only wanted to uncover her money.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ –
phrases.english: But isn't it he who raised the challenge and he who answered it –
phrases.notes: "He" is רב המנונא; he gave his own answer to his question.

phrases.english: it is about one who sells his field because of its poor quality?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב המנונא's challenge in step 12, which keeps שמואל's rule and רב נחמן's teaching standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a special case (a poor-quality field)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows any sale document acquires without payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a seller eager to unload a poor field finishes the sale with the document alone; normal sales need payment, so רב נחמן's ruling is new.

steps.title: Another answer: the sale document was really a gift
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי (or רב ביבי in the name of רב נחמן) explains the ברייתא differently: the seller really meant to give the field as a gift, and wrote it as a sale only to give the receiver stronger rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: (רב ביבי ends this teaching in the name of רב נחמן.) And רב אשי said: He wanted to give it to him as a gift. So why did he write it for him in the language of a sale? To make the receiver's position stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain רב המנונא's ברייתא, where a document alone completes a 'sale.' The answer is that it was really a gift dressed up as a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said a שטר alone can complete a gift but not a sale. So if the 'sale' in the ברייתא was really a gift, the שטר works without any problem. The sale wording was used on purpose, because a sale document gives the receiver more protection than a gift document (for example, the seller must pay him back if a creditor takes the field).

keyTerms.meaning: Ends the teaching with this; adds a closing explanation
To make his position stronger; to give him better rights

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the field was actually sold. The point is that the giver wanted to make a gift, and only borrowed the wording of a sale to help the receiver.

phrases.aramaic: (רַב בִּיבִי מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן)
phrases.english: (Rav Beivai ends this teaching in the name of Rav Naḥman)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, the answer is said by רב ביבי or by רב אשי.

phrases.english: and Rav Ashi said:
He wanted to give it to him as a gift,
so why did he write it for him in the language of a sale?
In order to make his position stronger.
phrases.notes: He means the receiver. A sale document gives the buyer more protection than a gift document does.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּמַתָּנָה בִּקֵּשׁ לִיתְּנָהּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to רב המנונא's challenge, next to the answer in Step 13 (selling a field because it is poor).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'sale' in the ברייתא is really a gift.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that a שטר alone completes a real sale, which goes against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a gift written in sale language. A שטר alone completes a gift, so שמואל's rule still holds.

steps.title: Challenge from borrowing from a slave or a wife
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a man borrows from his slave and then frees him, or from his wife and then divorces her, they cannot collect from him. This seems to show we do say he only wanted to uncover hidden money, which goes against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If he borrowed from his slave and then freed him, or from his wife and then divorced her, they have no claim against him. What is the reason? Is it not because we say he only wanted to uncover the money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's ruling from Step 9 with a ברייתא about loans from a slave or a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן ruled that when a man sells a field to his wife, we do NOT say he only wanted to uncover her hidden money. But in this ברייתא, the man never has to repay the loan. The only reason seems to be that the 'loan' was just a way to bring hidden money into the open, which is exactly the reasoning רב נחמן rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: They challenged:
If he borrowed from his slave and then freed him;
or from his wife, and then divorced her –
they have no claim at all against him.
What is the reason?
Is it not because we say:
he only wanted to uncover the money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the שטר and goes back to attack רב נחמן's main ruling from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that we do not say the husband only wanted to uncover his wife's money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא frees the borrower from paying his slave or wife. The best reason for that is that we DO say he only wanted to uncover their money, which goes against רב נחמן.

steps.title: A loan is different: no one wants to be 'servant to the lender'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a loan is a special case. A man does not want to make himself a 'borrower who is a servant to the lender,' so we assume the loan was only a way to uncover the money. A sale has no such issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he does not want to make himself into 'the borrower is a servant to the lender.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן by showing why the loan case is different from the sale case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a loan there is an extra reason to say it was a trick: a man does not want to be in debt to his own slave or wife, as the פסוק says, 'the borrower is a servant to the lender.' So we assume he never meant a real loan. Selling a field does not put him under anyone, so there is no such reason, and the sale stands, as רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not comfortable for him; he does not want it
The borrower is a servant to the lender (משלי)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's rule stays in place: a sale to one's wife is real. Only a loan from a slave or wife is treated as a way to uncover money, because no one wants to be a 'servant to the lender.'

phrases.english: It is different there,
because he does not want to make himself into
'the borrower is a servant to the lender.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּלָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְשַׁוּוֹיֵיהּ נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 by showing that the loan case has a special reason that does not apply to a sale.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a loan has an extra reason (not wanting to be a 'servant to the lender') that a sale lacks.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about loans proves that we always say a deal with a wife or slave is only meant to uncover money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only in a loan do we say this, because of the shame of being in debt. In a sale we do not, so רב נחמן's ruling holds.

steps.title: רב הונא בר אבין's ruling: a wife acquires a field her husband sold her
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר אבין sends a ruling that a man who sells a field to his wife: she acquires it. His ruling continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר אבין sent a ruling: One who sells a field to his wife, she acquires it,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ruling from רב הונא בר אבין on the same topic. This step is setting up the next move, because the ruling keeps going after these words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling agrees with רב נחמן's basic point: a sale from a husband to his wife works, and she owns the field. The comma at the end shows that more is coming, probably an added detail or condition about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent (a ruling, usually from ארץ ישראל)
She has acquired it; she owns it

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Avin sent a ruling:
One who sells a field to his wife – she has acquired it,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַב הוּנָא בַּר אָבִין: הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֶה לְאִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב נחמן, the גמרא brings a new ruling on the same case of a man selling a field to his wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a man sells a field to his wife, she acquires it (the ruling continues in the next part of the גמרא).
